correctness.rationale: The source's lobe-selection and vertical-width argument gives the exact upper bound H_n. For the matching lower bound, the boundary-distance derivative reduces to comparison with J(theta)=r(theta)sin(n theta)/sin((n+1)theta). A direct differentiation shows that J is strictly decreasing because tan(n theta)>n tan(theta) on 0<theta<pi/(2n). At alpha_n=pi/[2(n+1)], J(alpha_n)=c_n, so the distance to the proposed center has its global boundary minimum there and equals H_n. The n=1 case is the disk B(1,1). The asymptotic correction follows from the exact formula by Taylor expansion.

value.rationale: The roots-of-unity polynomial is the canonical obstruction in the deterministic inradius problem, appearing in the original 1958 formulation and in the 2026 sharp asymptotic theorem. Its exact finite-degree inradius is therefore a natural invariant. The result proves that the lead source's width obstruction is attained, identifies an explicit maximizing disk and tangency pair, and quantifies the finite-degree approach to the sharp asymptotic scale. This is a complete model classification rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
